citation: Özgökmen, T. M., W. E. Johns, H. Peters and S. Matt (2003), Turbulent Mixing in the Red Sea Outflow Plume from a High-Resolution Nonhydrostatic Model, Journal of Physical Oceanography 33, 1846–1869

source_identity.rights: American Meteorological Society, 2003. No redistribution permission inferred; original and page renders remain private.

review_scope.text_search_scope: All 24 pages searched for width and lateral confinement; search hits alone are not measurement admissions.

findings.finding: Approximately 100 km length and 3 km width at overflow depth describe the Northern Channel.
findings.consequence: Retain bathymetric context, not a whole-current dimension or paired velocity-edge measurement.

findings.finding: The winter investigation concerns one confined branch after the overflow splits.
findings.consequence: Neither dimension represents all Red Sea outflow branches or downstream spreading.

findings.finding: The model resolves along-channel and vertical dynamics; lateral edge effects and canyon-wall intrusions are omitted.
findings.consequence: Its two-dimensional solution does not recover lateral velocity boundaries.

findings.finding: The highlighted paths are schematic branch and station context.
findings.consequence: No observed current axis, footprint or length digitized from this figure.

cross_source_rule.rule: Do not combine the 3 km and prior 5 km channel descriptions into a current-width uncertainty or seasonal envelope. Matching sections, depth definitions, measurement methods and dates have not been established.

next_measurement_gate: Recover dated cross-flow velocity sections with both lateral plume boundaries and depth/layer support; admit branch scope before attributing any result to the parent current.
